lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedThe Wing That Formed Too LateMinor DefeatThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Market Garden's reach for Arnhem was scaled back before it happened rather than mourned after: Browning's private reservation taken seriously instead of overruled. The Scheldt was cleared before the autumn's offensives rather than after: Antwerp opened weeks early, and the priority error most postwar assessments rank among the campaign's costliest was simply not made. The fleet was kept at Alexandria while Crete fell, the cruisers saved and the Army left to remember it: the island fell in days, with a large part of the garrison taken prisoner. No branch of this campaign reaches a different destination: the war's outcome was decided by arithmetic no single conference or campaign could overturn.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
